title: Destroying and Preserving Measurement Incompatibility over a Quantum Channel
abstract: A quantum channel is called incompatibility-breaking if it always destroys the incompatibility of quantum measurements. On the other extreme are incompatibility-preserving channels, which never destroy incompatibility. This work studies both types of channels through the mathematical framework of zonotopes and zonoids, an approach that provides a complete characterization of compatibility for dichotomic measurements and is particularly powerful in the qubit setting. Using the language of zonoids, we present necessary and sufficient conditions for when a qubit unital channel is incompatibility-breaking, which are also sufficient for nonunital channels. As one of our main results, we demonstrate the superactivation phenomenon of two incompatibility-breaking qubit channels that are no longer incompatibility-breaking when used in parallel. Translating this result into the task of quantum steering, it says that two copies of a two-qubit Werner state can be steered at noise threshold $1/2$, even though this is impossible using just one copy. For the problem of incompatibility preservation, we prove that a quantum channel with matching input and output dimensions will preserve general incompatibility if and only if it is a unitary transformation. When the output dimension is larger, this result no longer holds, and we offer a conjectured form of a general incompatibility-preserving channel.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes quantum channels based on whether they destroy or preserve measurement incompatibility. It utilizes the mathematical theory of zonotopes and zonoids to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for these behaviors in the qubit setting. The results provide deep insights into the fundamental limitations and capabilities of quantum information processing channels.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental properties of quantum channels regarding their ability to destroy or preserve the incompatibility of quantum measurements.
main_result: It establishes that for channels with matching input/output dimensions, incompatibility preservation is equivalent to the channel being unitary, and it derives necessary and sufficient conditions for a qubit channel to be incompatibility-breaking.
method: The work employs advanced mathematical tools, specifically the geometric framework of zonotopes and zonoids, to translate the quantum compatibility problem into a problem of convex geometry.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general quantum channels (CPTP maps) acting on qubits, analyzing measurement assemblages (POVMs) and their associated compatibility structures.
key_observables: Measurement incompatibility, compatibility, quantum steering correlations, and the structure of the generating zonoid measure.
important_parameters: The channel type (unital vs. nonunital), the dimension matching between input and output, and the noise threshold ($r=1/2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mathematical machinery of zonoid representation theorems and the assumption of operational equivalence between different formulations of POVMs.
paper_structure: The paper systematically defines incompatibility-breaking/preserving channels, develops the mathematical link using zonoids, derives conditions for qubit channels, and proves the unitary characterization for preservation.
why_interesting: The geometric approach using zonoids provides a powerful, rigorous mathematical tool to characterize fundamental resource properties (like incompatibility) in quantum channels, which is highly relevant for understanding noise and quantum communication protocols.
